root_cause.text: The bounds check for 128-byte SQE operations in io_init_req() used the logical SQ head position (`ctx->cached_sq_head`) instead of the physical SQE index, enabling an attacker to remap via `sq_array` to the last physical slot and cause an out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the condition from `!(ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1))` to `(unsigned)(sqe - ctx->sq_sqes) >= ctx->sq_entries - 1`, and the CVE description confirms that setting `sq_array[N] = sq_entries - 1` places a 128-byte operation at the last physical SQE slot, leading to a 64-byte overread in `io_uring_cmd_sqe_copy()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the boundary check for mixed SQ operations to use the actual SQE index rather than the cached head position.
intent_record.what: Changed the condition in io_init_req from `!(ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1))` to `(unsigned)(sqe - ctx->sq_sqes) >= ctx->sq_entries - 1`.
intent_record.how: The new condition checks if the current SQE is at the last position in the SQ ring (or beyond) by comparing its index to `sq_entries - 1`. This correctly identifies when a mixed 128b operation cannot be satisfied because it requires two contiguous entries but the current entry is the last one. The old condition incorrectly used the cached head position, which could either miss or falsely trigger the failure.
